title: Equivariant curve-pencil preparation over a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a normal proper geometrically integral finite-type $k$-scheme of dimension $d\geq2$, and let a finite group $H$ act on $X$ and $k$ compatibly with the structure morphism. The action need not be faithful. There are normal proper geometrically integral finite-type $k$-schemes $X'$ and $Y$, with compatible $H$-actions, an $H$-equivariant H-projective surjective birational morphism $\pi:X'\to X$, and an $H$-equivariant H-projective dominant morphism $g:X'\to Y$. The scheme $Y$ is projective and geometrically integral over $k$ of dimension $d-1$, and the generic fibre of $g$ is a geometrically integral curve. Birational here means that $\pi$ is an isomorphism over a dense open of $X$ and identifies the function fields. No smoothness of this generic curve is asserted.

Field, integrality, properness, finite type, geometric integrality, dimension, H-projectivity, finite morphisms, surjectivity and function fields use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and [def-sc-function-field]. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target.

proof.text: Put $E=k(X)$. Its affine fraction-field description and the finite-type dimension formula give finite generation over $k$ and $\operatorname{trdeg}_kE=d$. Transfer geometric integrality from a nonempty affine of $X$ to $\operatorname{Spec}E$, so $E\otimes_kK$ is a domain for every $K/k$. The induced semilinear action on $E$ therefore satisfies the invariant-parameter lemma. Choose its full separating family $t_1,\ldots,t_d$, and put $F=k(t_1,\ldots,t_{d-1})$; $E/F$ has separating basis $t_d$.

source.place: Lemma 5.2 proof, printed p.613; field-base assembly of the extracted arguments (local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online)

proof.text: Apply semilinear equivariant Chow modification to $X$, giving an integral projective $T$ with equivariant birational $p:T\to X$. Apply the normalization lemma to $(T,p,X)$: $X$ is normal, proper and geometrically integral, so it gives a normal projective geometrically integral $N$ with equivariant H-projective surjective birational $p_1:N\to X$ and the same field $E$.

source.place: Lemma 5.2 proof, printed p.613; field-base assembly of the extracted arguments (local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online)

proof.text: Apply the invariant normalized-graph lemma to $N$ and $t_1,\ldots,t_{d-1}$. It gives normal projective geometrically integral $X'$, an equivariant birational H-projective $a:X'\to N$, and a dominant equivariant H-projective $b:X'\to P=\mathbf P^{d-1}_k$ inducing $F\subseteq E$. Set $\pi=p_1a$; composition preserves H-projectivity. Its maps are surjective, its function-field map is the identity, and intersecting their isomorphism opens gives a dense open of $X$ over which $\pi$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 5.2 proof, printed p.613; field-base assembly of the extracted arguments (local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online)

proof.text: Apply the equivariant projective Stein lemma to $b$. It gives $X'\xrightarrow{g}Y\xrightarrow{q}P$ with $Y$ normal projective geometrically integral, $g$ dominant H-projective, compatible actions, and $L=k(Y)$ finite over $F$ and algebraically closed in $E$. All schemes are of finite type and proper over $k$.

source.place: Lemma 5.2 proof, printed p.613; field-base assembly of the extracted arguments (local PDF WANTED; publisher PDF read online)

proof.text: Use the separating-Stein generic-curve lemma for $k\subseteq F\subseteq L\subseteq E$ and $g$: Step 1 supplies separable generation and relative transcendence degree one, and Step 4 supplies the constant-field hypotheses. It gives the geometrically integral proper generic curve of dimension one and $\dim Y=\operatorname{trdeg}_kF=d-1$. Together with $\pi$ and the actions these are every asserted clause.
